description.narrative:
National Democratic Institute (NDI) har ansökt om finansiering på 13 601 800 SEK för att genomföra projektet "Advancing Gender Equality through Women’s Political Participation" i Nordmakedonien under perioden 2020-2023.
Projektets syfte är att minska de institutionella, sociokulturella och individuella hindren för kvinnors egenmakt och därigenom öka kvinnors meningsfulla politiska deltagande samt främja jämställdhet på lokal nivå och inom de politiska partierna.
Insatsen ämnar att - förbättra jämställdheten inom politiska partier genom att bidra till att övervinna interna hinder som hämmar kvinnors politiska deltagande och ledarskap. Detta inkluderar aktiviteter för att öka medvetenheten om vikten av och fördelarna med att integrera jämställdhet inom partistrukturerna. Att bygga kapacitet hos politiskt aspirerande unga kvinnor och män att ta ledarpositioner inom politiska partier är ett mervärde som väntas intensifiera ovanstående process.
- ge kvinnliga kandidater kompetens att framgångsrikt bedriva kampanjer under lokalvalet 2021 och att styra på lokal nivå. Utbildning inom förvaltningsarbete ska tillhandahållas för de framröstade kvinnliga politikerna för att förse dem med färdigheter för att kunna utföra sina roller.
- minska 'våldet mot kvinnor i politiken' (VAW-P) genom att använda information från forskning som visar omfattningen och djupet av VAW-P. Informationen ska ge vägledning till kommuner som antar jämställdhetsfunktioner och jämställdhetskommittéer för att skapa trygga miljöer för kvinnor att utöva ledarskap och beslutsfattande makt. Allmänhetens medvetenhet och utbildning om VAW-P kommer belysas genom kampanjen "It´s Not OK".
Insatsens projektlängd är 32 månader och den begärda budgeten uppgår till 13 601 800 SEK.

The National Democratic Institute has applied to Sida for funding of 13 601 800 SEK to carry out the "Advancing Gender Equality through Women’s Political Participation" in North Macedonia during the period 2020-2023.
The project aim is to reduce the institutional, socio-cultural and individual barriers to women's empowerment, and thereby to increase women's meaningful political participation and to advance gender equality at local governance level and within the political parties.
The proposed concept is set to: - Improve gender equality in political parties, by supporting in overcoming the internal barriers that impede women's political participation and leadership. Raising awareness on the importance and the benefits in streamlining the gender equality within the political party structures would be attended through cross-section work with the political parties. Building capacity for politically aspirant young women and men to take leadership positions within political parties is an added value that would intensify the above process. - Provide women candidates with the skills to campaign successfully during the local elections in 2021 and to govern at the local level. Good governance practices training shall be provided for the elected women officials in order to equip them with skills to ably carry out their roles. - Reduce violence against women in politics (VAW-P), by utilizing the information of the research undertaken under USAID funding on the scope and depth of VAW-P to provide guidance to municipalities that enact gender focal points and equal opportunity committees to create safe local governance environments for women to exercise leadership and decision-making power. Public awareness raising and education on VAW-P shall be attended through implementing the "It's Not OK" campaign.
The suggested program duration is 32 months and the requested budget is 13 601 800 SEK.

The project Advancing Gender Equality through Women Political Participation - WoMenLead, was focusing on the political parties, local authorities, youth and individual women candidates for leadership positions in politics, as well as the general public. The aim was to reduce stereotypes, support advancement of women in politics and to combat violence against women participation in politics.
The project's overall goal was to lower the individual, socio-cultural, and institutional barriers to women's political participation through a series of interrelated interventions.
The project objectives were to:
- Improve gender equality in political parties by working with a cross-section of political parties to raise their awareness of the importance and benefits of streamlining gender equality within political party structures
- Provide women candidates with the skills and a supportive environment to campaign successfully for and govern at the local level and in the Parliament , by providing technical assistance to women candidates for municipal councils, mayoral positions and at the positions as members of Parliament, training the elected women officials in good governance practices in order to equip them with the skills to ably carry out their roles
- Reduce violence against women in politics focusing on the periods during the municipal, Presidential and Parliamentarian elections.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
The program achieved important results in a difficult context and a sensitive area of support.
From Sida's perspective the results that substantially contributed to achieving project objectives include:
- Several of the political parties that benefited from the training organized by the WoMenLead project decided to initiate and institute a Womens Leadership Academy for the members of their own political political party (DUI, Alternativa, SDSM, VMRO-DPMNE), These Academies would contribute to long-term capacity building and commitment of these political parties to stimulate and achieve gender equality .
- In December 2022 the parliamentary Committee on European Affairs passed amendments to the Criminal Code, which included the amendment on the Workplace Harassment Protection Act, that was prepared by LAG Agro Leader (WoMenLead project cooperating CSO). The WoMenLead project provided support in advocating for this amendment to the Law by using the established cooperation with the members of Parliament.
- The above decision was strengthened by adopting Gender equality measures by five political parties/coalition to be part of their election platform.
Further, the results achieved include:
- A Code of Conduct for fair and democratic elections and committing that with their election activities they will make sure to protect the fundamental values was signed by 15 out of planned 17 political parties - reaching 75% of political parties which adhere to the Code of Conduct.
- A total number of 80 media including print news, online news portal, online news, radio stations and television stations signed the Code of Conduct for ethical reporting during ahead of elections , resulting with full implementation and no violations to the Code of Conduct reported by the Macedonian Agency of Audio Visual and Visual Services during the local elections.
- A total number of 25 women (72 %) that were trained through WoMenLead project were nominated as candidates for local and parliamentary elections (percentage reached in Y1-Y5 of project implementation period).
- To raise awareness and reduce violence against women during the election period two Media campaigns were organized under the brand "Vote NO for violence against women in politics" in 2021 for the local elections and again in 2024 for Presidential and Parliamentary elections. These campaigns have reached high visibility and interaction level. For the media campaign in 2021 materials were shown on 13 TV channels across the country; engaged with by citizens through social media platforms such as Twitter and Instagram; as well as featured in articles within online and print news sources, as well as on news portals. The media campaign in 2024 took place primarily on Facebook and Instagram, but it was also present on TV and radio.
An unexpected positive result stems from the established strong cooperation and networking of Sida supported projects in gender equality area and their synergizing and mutual support to reach the target. In this case NDI has actively supported UN Women in advocacy for gender responsive budgeting by engaging the women parliamentarians in support to the change of the Organic Budget Law and further promoting gender responsive budgeting in the communication with cooperating municipal authorities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
